Random Variable Algebra: Mini Project 10

Jason M. Klemm

2026-04-05

Given Information

Suppose \(Y_i \sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,M)\) and a sample size of \(n=10\) is made with \(M=200\).

Part 1

What is the algebraic expression for the pdf of \(Y_{max}\), which is \(f_{Y_{max}}(y)\)?

To solve this we need to first define what \(f_{Y_{max}}(y)\) is:1

\[ f_{Y_{max}}(y) = f_{Y'_n}(y)=n[F_Y(y)]^{n-1}f_Y(y) \]

Now what we need to do is find \(f_Y(y)\) and \(F_Y(y)\) given our information:

\[ f_Y(y)=\frac{1}{b-a}=\frac{1}{200-0}=\frac{1}{200} \]

\[ F_Y(y)=\int_0^y\frac{1}{200}dt = \left[\frac{t}{200}\right]_0^y=\frac{y}{200} \]

Next we plug in all of our values and get the algebraic expression for \(f_{Y_{max}}(y)\) as:

\[ f_{Y_{max}}(y) = f_{Y'_{10}}(y)=10\left(\frac{y}{200}\right)^{9}\frac{1}{200} = \frac{10y^9}{200^{10}} \]

Therefore:

\[ f_{Y_{max}}(y) = \frac{10y^9}{200^{10}} \]

Part 2

What is the algebraic expression for the pdf of \(Y_{min}\), which is \(f_{Y_{min}}(y)\)?

To solve this we need to first define what \(f_{Y_{min}}(y)\) is:1

\[ f_{Y_{min}}(y) = f_{Y'_1}(y)=n[1-F_Y(y)]^{n-1}f_Y(y) \]

Using the results for \(f_Y(y)\) and \(F_Y(y)\) from Part 1 we have:

\[ f_{Y_{min}}(y) = f_{Y'_{1}}(y)=10\left(1-\frac{y}{200}\right)^{9}\frac{1}{200} = \frac{1}{20}\left(1-\frac{y}{200}\right)^{9} \]

Therefore:

\[ f_{Y_{min}}(y) = \frac{1}{20}\left(1-\frac{y}{200}\right)^{9} \]

Part 3A/C

Make functions for expressions in Part 1 and Part 2:

# Ymax from Part 1
algeYmax <- function(y){
  
  10*y**9/(200**10)
  
}

# Ymin from Part 2
algeYmin <- function(y){
  
  (1/20)*(1-(y/200))**9
  
}

The function was taken from the given script on canvas and edited here:

ymax <- function(n,iter, mi,M, title){
  y <- runif(n = iter*n, 
             min = mi,
             max = M) # random vector from uniform
  data <- matrix(data = y,
                 nrow = n, 
                 ncol = iter) # Holds simulated data
  MM <- apply(X = data, 
              MARGIN = 2, 
              FUN = max) # apply max() to the columns of data
  
  hist(x = MM, 
       xlab = "Simulated maximum value of the sample", 
       main = title, freq= FALSE)
  
  invisible(list(maxun = MM)) # invisible list
  
}

Generate all plots for \(Y_{max}\):

# iter = 1000
ymax(n = 10, iter = 1000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymax order stats - iter = 1000")
curve(algeYmax(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)

# iter = 10000
ymax(n = 10, iter = 10000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymax order stats - iter = 10000")
curve(algeYmax(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)

# iter = 100000
ymax(n = 10, iter = 100000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymax order stats - iter = 100000")
curve(algeYmax(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)

Part 3B/C

The function was taken from the given script on canvas and edited here:

ymin <- function(n,iter, mi,M, title){
  y <- runif(n = iter*n, 
             min = mi,
             max = M) # random vector from uniform
  data <- matrix(data = y,
                 nrow = n, 
                 ncol = iter) # Holds simulated data
  MinM <- apply(X = data, 
              MARGIN = 2, 
              FUN = min) # apply max() to the columns of data
  
  hist(x = MinM, 
       xlab = "Simulated minimum value of the sample", 
       main = title, freq= FALSE)
  
  invisible(list(minun = MinM)) # invisible list
  
}

Generate all plots for \(Y_{min}\):

# iter = 1000
ymin(n = 10, iter = 1000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymin order stats - iter = 1000")
curve(algeYmin(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)

# iter = 10000
ymin(n = 10, iter = 10000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymin order stats - iter = 10000")
curve(algeYmin(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)

# iter = 100000
ymin(n = 10, iter = 100000, mi = 0,M = 200, title = "Ymin order stats - iter = 100000")
curve(algeYmin(x),from = 0, to = 200, add = TRUE)
